title: PostgreSQL: table dropdown empty, code-editor works
body:
### What happened?

- I clicked on the table selector in the query builder (PostgreSQL)
- Nothing happened (empty dropdown) even though the database connection works
- Enter the table name manually is also not possible

### What did you expect to happen?

The available tables are shown in the dropdown in the query builder

### Did this work before?

In previous grafana versions there was an old / another query builder

### How do we reproduce it?

- I added a postgresql datasource via provisioned datasource:
```
apiVersion: 1
datasources:
- name: TestDB
  type: postgres
  orgId: 1
  uid: postgres_test
  url: postgres:5432
  database: TestDB
  user: test
  secureJsonData:
    password: "test"
  jsonData:
    sslmode: "disable"
    postgresVersion: 1300
    timescaledb: false
```

- I opened the explorer tab with this datasource. 


- I added the same datasource manually in the GUI of grafana
- I opened the explorer tab and clicked on the table selector

### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel?

_No response_

### Environment (with versions)?

Grafana: 10.3.3
OS: Windows (grafana in docker, WSL)
Browser: Firefox 123


### Grafana platform?

Docker

### Datasource(s)?

PostgreSQL

comments.body:
thanks for all the info @reporter . unfortunately i still cannot reproduce it (i tried postgres 13, works here).

the sql query that retrieves the tables to put into the table-dropdown is this:
```sql
select quote_ident(table_name) as "table" from information_schema.tables
    where quote_ident(table_schema) not in ('information_schema',
                             'pg_catalog',
                             '_timescaledb_cache',
                             '_timescaledb_catalog',
                             '_timescaledb_internal',
                             '_timescaledb_config',
                             'timescaledb_information',
                             'timescaledb_experimental')
      and 
          quote_ident(table_schema) IN (
          SELECT
            CASE WHEN trim(s[i]) = '"$user"' THEN user ELSE trim(s[i]) END
          FROM
            generate_series(
              array_lower(string_to_array(current_setting('search_path'),','),1),
              array_upper(string_to_array(current_setting('search_path'),','),1)
            ) as i,
            string_to_array(current_setting('search_path'),',') s
          )
```
could you try running it in the code-editor? does it return the correct table-names? does it return an empty result? an error?

comments.body:
Are you sure that you can't reproduce it?

Look at the output of the api endpoint `/api/datasources`. You'll notice that the manually added datasource has the `database` field inside `jsonData`.

So if you provision by file, add the `database` field inside `jsonData`, not outside and it will work.

Is this a documentation issue?

comments.author: reporter
participant7
comments.body:
> Are you sure that you can't reproduce it?
> 
> Look at the output of the api endpoint `/api/datasources`. You'll notice that the manually added datasource has the `database` field inside `jsonData`.
> 
> So if you provision by file, add the `database` field inside `jsonData`, not outside and it will work.
> 
> Is this a documentation issue?

In my case, this worked a charm. I had `database` as a field on the top level object. After moving it to `jsonData`, the table names were correctly shown in the dropdown.

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
This also works, for me.

It's worth noting that the current (v11.2) [documentation](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/v11.2/datasources/postgres/#provision-the-data-source) also has the `database` field under `jsonData`.

In earlier versions this was documented differently, with the field being at the top level of the datasource. E.g. [v8.5 documentation](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/v8.5/datasources/postgres/#configure-the-data-source-with-provisioning).

Edit: It seems that the field moved to `jsonData` in the [documentation of v9.4](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/v9.4/datasources/postgres/#provision-the-data-source).
